docs.grippable.component: `Grippable` says whose hands may PICK a subtree up — the permission twin of `Private`: privacy
cuts what a seat SEES, grip cuts what a seat may MOVE. `by` lists the seats that may lift; the
empty list is locked to everyone (a fixed board element), and a node under no grip at all is the
open desk, liftable by anyone.
```ts
import { node, Container, Grippable, grippableBy } from "game-kit"
const hand = node("northHand",
Container({ layout: "row" }),
Grippable({ by: ["north"] }))     // every card in it is north's to lift
grippableBy(cardInHand, "north")    // true
grippableBy(cardInHand, "south")    // false — the subtree cut
## It cuts a SUBTREE
Like privacy, grip is a fact of the TREE: a gripped container grips everything in it, so a card
cannot be freely grabbed out of someone else's hand — and the cards themselves never carry the
atom. Lifting a card OUT of the hand and onto the desk is what frees it, exactly as detaching
starts a shadow: the tree is the switch.
## The wiring asks, the atom answers
`grippableBy(node, seat)` is the whole runtime: the drag wiring adds it beside `draggable` as
the pick's gate, and the other player's hand refuses the finger before anything lifts. No
permission flag lives on the card, and there is nothing to unset when a hand changes owners —
rewrite `by` on the hand and every card follows.
docs.grippable.hands: Two hands and your seat. Pick `seat` and drag: your own hand's cards lift, the other hand's
refuse the finger — the grip cuts the subtree, so the refusing cards never carried the atom.
The open card in the middle lifts for either seat (no grip — the open desk), and the pale mark
refuses both: its `by` is the empty list, a board element locked to everyone.
